_note: 일반적인 재활 진행 단계를 콘텐츠 초안용으로 정리한 것. 게시 전 원우 님(재활 전공)이 반드시 검토·수정. 의료 조언이 아님.

phases.name: Phase 1 · Protect & activate (days 1–7)
drills: Gentle hip hinge with no load
Walking at normal pace, no running

phases.name: Phase 2 · Rebuild strength & length (weeks 2–4)
drills: Sliding leg curls on a towel or slider

phases.name: Phase 3 · Return to sprinting (weeks 4+)
drills: Deceleration and change-of-direction drills at full speed

hamstring.content_angle: Why hamstrings tear at sprint speed, and why Nordic curls are the single most proven prevention drill.
hamstring.red_flags: A pop felt at the moment of injury, large bruising or inability to walk means imaging first; recurrence risk is highest when players return too early.

phases.name: Phase 1 · Post-surgery basics (weeks 0–6)
drills: Heel slides for knee bend, patella mobilisation
Short-arc leg extension with no load

phases.name: Phase 2 · Strength & balance (months 2–5)
drills: Split squats and step-ups, slow and controlled
Single-leg balance on an unstable surface
Leg press building to body-weight equivalent

phases.name: Phase 3 · Plyometrics & return to play (months 6–9+)
drills: Double-leg → single-leg hops with soft landings
Cutting and pivot drills, planned then reactive

knee_acl.content_angle: ACL rehab is a 9-month project: show what month 1, month 4 and month 8 look like, and why the landing mechanics matter more than the surgery.
knee_acl.red_flags: Swelling that returns, the knee giving way or locking means stop and see the surgeon; return-to-play tests, not the calendar, decide readiness.

phases.name: Phase 1 · Settle & activate
drills: Stationary bike, no resistance, for range
Calf raises to keep the lower leg working

phases.name: Phase 2 · Strength
drills: Wall sits and goblet squats to pain-free depth

knee_other.content_angle: The knee is usually the victim: show how the hip and ankle take load off it.
knee_other.red_flags: Locking, giving way or significant swelling needs imaging.

phases.name: Phase 1 · Protect & move (days 1–7)
drills: Weight-bearing as tolerated, seated calf raises

phases.name: Phase 2 · Strength & balance (weeks 2–4)
drills: Standing calf raises, double → single leg

ankle.content_angle: Most ankle sprains come back because balance training gets skipped: show the 3 balance drills every footballer should do.
ankle.red_flags: Inability to take 4 steps, bone tenderness or a syndesmosis (high ankle) sprain means imaging and a longer timeline.

phases.name: Phase 1 · Calm it down
drills: Adductor isometric squeeze with a ball, 5×30s
Hip flexor and adductor gentle mobility

phases.name: Phase 2 · Strength
drills: Copenhagen plank, short lever → long lever

groin.content_angle: The Copenhagen plank cut groin injuries by ~40% in studies. Show the 3 levels.
groin.red_flags: Pain with coughing or deep core pressure can mean a sports hernia rather than a muscle strain.

phases.name: Phase 2 · Strength
drills: Standing calf raises, double → single leg, slow eccentric

calf.content_angle: Calf injuries climb after 28: show why soleus strength (bent-knee raises) is the missing piece.
calf.red_flags: Sudden calf pain with swelling or warmth needs a check for a clot before any rehab.

phases.name: Phase 1 · Medical phase (surgery or boot, weeks 0–8)
drills: Toe and knee range of motion
Upper-body and core training to stay fit

phases.name: Phase 2 · Tendon loading (months 2–5)
drills: Seated → standing calf raises, slow heavy
Heel raises off a step, eccentric focus

achilles.content_angle: Achilles ruptures end careers when the tendon never gets heavy slow loading back: show the progression.
achilles.red_flags: A rupture is a surgical/medical decision; any content must stay educational.

quad.content_angle: Rectus femoris strains come from shooting: show the reverse Nordic and the kicking progression.
quad.red_flags: A visible gap or bulge in the muscle needs imaging.

hip.content_angle: Hip strength protects the knee and the groin: 3 glute drills.
hip.red_flags: Deep groin pinch with hip flexion can be labral; imaging decides.

phases.name: Phase 1 · Protect (boot / limited load)
drills: Toe mobility within the boot's limits

phases.name: Phase 2 · Foot strength
drills: Calf raises progressing to single leg

foot.content_angle: Metatarsal fractures are the classic 'boot and wait' injury: show what to train while in the boot.
foot.red_flags: Bone healing timelines are set by imaging, not feel.

phases.name: Phase 3 · Load & rotate
drills: Pallof press and rotational med-ball throws

back.content_angle: Back pain in footballers is usually a hip-mobility and core-control problem: 3 drills.
back.red_flags: Leg numbness, weakness or bladder changes are emergencies.

shoulder.content_angle: Shoulder injuries don't stop leg training: show the 'train around it' week.
shoulder.red_flags: Dislocations and fractures follow the surgeon's timeline.

phases.name: Stage 1 · Rest & symptom-limited activity (24–48h)
drills: Screen and noise limits as advised

phases.name: Stage 2 · Light aerobic → sport-specific
drills: Stationary bike at low heart rate

concussion.content_angle: Educational only: explain the graded return-to-play protocol. No exercise 'recommendations'.
concussion.red_flags: Worsening headache, vomiting, confusion or drowsiness are emergencies. Never give training advice for a head injury.

phases.name: Phase 1 · Protect & isometrics
drills: Pain-free isometric holds for the affected muscle

phases.name: Phase 2 · Eccentric strength
drills: Slow eccentric loading of the muscle

muscle_general.content_angle: Follow-up post once the club confirms the exact muscle.
muscle_general.red_flags: Wait for the specific diagnosis before any detailed content.
